Top marker genes per group

Source: R/dot_plots.R
top_markers.Rd

Picks the top marker genes of each group from Seurat::FindAllMarkers() output (or any DE table with a group column), as a named list for the `features` of DotPlot_bioToolkit.

Usage

top_markers(
  markers,
  n = 5,
  group.col = "cluster",
  rank.by = c("logfc", "padj"),
  padj.cutoff = 0.05,
  unique = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

markers

A data frame of markers, e.g. from Seurat::FindAllMarkers(); read with standardize_de

n

Number of genes per group, default is 5

group.col

Column naming the group of each row, default is "cluster" (as FindAllMarkers)

rank.by

How genes are ranked within a group: "logfc" (default; largest log2 fold change, ties broken by the adjusted p-value) or "padj" (smallest adjusted p-value, ties broken by the largest log2 fold change). Ranking by p-value favours broadly expressed genes in large groups; ranking by fold change favours specific genes

padj.cutoff

Only genes with an adjusted p-value below this, and a positive log2 fold change, are markers. Default is 0.05

unique

Whether each gene is a marker of one group only, default is TRUE: a gene that is a marker of several groups is kept for the group where its log2 fold change is largest

...

Further arguments to standardize_de, e.g. `feature.col`

Value

A named list of character vectors, one per group with markers, in the order of the groups

See also

DotPlot_bioToolkit

Examples

markers <- data.frame(
    gene = c("Cd3e", "Cd3d", "Ms4a1", "Cd79a", "Cd3e"),
    cluster = factor(c("T", "T", "B", "B", "B")),
    avg_log2FC = c(3, 2.5, 4, 3.5, 0.5),
    p_val = 1e-10, p_val_adj = 1e-8
)
top_markers(markers, n = 2)
#> $B
#> [1] "Ms4a1" "Cd79a"
#> 
#> $T
#> [1] "Cd3e" "Cd3d"
#>
